question: Passing a mixture through a column of porous beads so its components are held back by different amounts is _____, and what the beads are made of decides what it sorts by.
questions: In the gel filtration form of _____ the small molecules linger inside the beads while the large ones flow past, so the biggest leave the column first.
Measuring a mixture measures an average, so _____ is now the front half of nearly every method that reports on individual molecules.
abstract:
Chromatography separates a mixture by passing it through a column packed with a porous solid matrix, in which the different components are retarded to different extents and can be collected separately as they flow out of the bottom. What the matrix is made of decides what the column sorts by: charge in ion-exchange chromatography, exposed hydrophobic regions in hydrophobic chromatography, size in gel filtration, and the ability to bind a particular molecule in affinity chromatography. Gel filtration is the one worth thinking through, since its beads are porous and small molecules linger inside them while larger ones stay in the flowing solvent between, so the biggest leave the column first. Charge can also be used without a column at all, and in electrophoresis an electric field moves a protein at a rate set by its net charge, its size and its shape, which SDS polyacrylamide-gel electrophoresis turned into routine analysis in the mid-1960s. Before any of that, whole organelles are sorted by differential centrifugation, a method developed by Albert Claude, Christian de Duve and their colleagues in the 1940s and 1950s that separates components by size and density.

Separation is now almost always the front half of a measurement rather than an end in itself. Lipidomics is the clear case, resting on advances in mass spectrometry, chromatography and computational analysis together, which is what has allowed lipid networks to be mapped at high resolution across molecular, cellular and organismal scales. A working study now combines several such methods at once, one recent example pairing liquid chromatography and mass spectrometry for metabolites with non-reducing tandem mass tag proteomics in the same cells. What that buys is not only sensitivity, since electrospray mass spectrometry captures the states actually present in a sample rather than an average over them. Optical methods that report an ensemble average can struggle to resolve those states at all, which is the whole argument for separating a mixture before asking anything of it.
